description: Defines a full-length AFOQT practice exam mode with Beginner, Advanced, and Expert variants. Each run simulates the real AFOQT timing and section order, randomly drawing questions from the existing question-bank JSON files across all subtopics and parts. Sections are timed, and composites (Verbal, Quantitative, Academic Aptitude, Pilot, CSO, ABM) are computed from the relevant subtests.

beginner.summary: Use only beginner-difficulty questions from each subtest's pools.
beginner.sectionSequence: Use the exact AFOQT section order shown in examSections, but always pull from beginner difficulty pools.

advanced.summary: Use only advanced-difficulty questions from each subtest's pools.
advanced.sectionSequence: Same section order and timing as real AFOQT, but questions pulled from advanced difficulty pools.

expert.summary: Use only expert-difficulty questions from each subtest's pools.
expert.sectionSequence: Same section order and timing as real AFOQT, but questions pulled from expert difficulty pools.

selectionDetails.subtopicPool: ALL verbal_analogies subtopics for chosen difficulty
selectionDetails.rule: Distribute draws as evenly as possible across all subtopics. On each exam run, randomize both subtopic order and question ids. Do not repeat any question id within a single exam run.

selectionDetails.subtopicPool: ratio_and_proportion, percent_problems, fractions_and_decimals, time_rates_work, probability, algebra, averages, mixed_word_problems
selectionDetails.rule: Attempt to pull a roughly equal number of questions from each AR subtopic. If 25 does not divide evenly, randomly allocate the extra questions across random subtopics.
Sample uniformly across all vocab subtopics and difficulty pool; balance synonyms vs antonyms questions.

selectionDetails.subtopicPool: ALL Math Knowledge subtopics for chosen difficulty (order_of_operations, number_sets, fractions, decimals, ratio_and_proportion, percent_problems, exponents_and_roots, algebra_basics, evaluating_expressions, solving_linear_equations, functions, function_evaluation, slope, graphing_linear_functions, coordinate_geometry, polygons_and_angles, circles, transformations, sequences, probability, statistics, etc.)
selectionDetails.rule: Treat each MK subtopic as an equal-weight bucket. For 25 total questions, repeatedly select a random subtopic, then a random unused question from either its part1 or part2 file, until 25 questions are assembled with no duplicates.

selectionDetails.passagePool: For chosen difficulty, use the appropriate passage-number range (e.g., beginner: 1–20).
selectionDetails.rule: Randomly sample 5 passages for this section; for each selected passage, include all 5 questions for that passage. Shuffle question order across passages.

selectionDetails.scenarioThemes: chain_of_command, teamwork, ethics, conflict_resolution, professionalism, safety
selectionDetails.rule: Randomly select scenarios so that major themes are represented approximately evenly. Each scenario contributes 1 scored question (single-best or best/worst); no duplicates in a single run.

Typically use a fixed inventory of 240 items. These are NOT included in composites and are not right/wrong scored – they are Likert-style responses for internal matching. App may present them for practice but keep them separate from score reports.

selectionDetails.subtopicPool: newtons_laws, forces_and_motion, energy_and_work, simple_machines, electricity_basics, magnetism_basics, waves_and_sound, basic_thermodynamics
selectionDetails.rule: Sample questions evenly across physics/chemistry subtopics; prefer conceptual and non-calculus-level numeric questions.

Build several table sets per difficulty, each with multiple questions. For the full practice exam, choose a small number of sets (e.g., 4–6) and include enough questions from those sets to total 40 items, emphasizing row/column lookup and simple comparisons.

Randomly choose instrument panel sets (attitude + heading + climb/descent). For each panel, generate one or more questions about aircraft attitude and heading. Ensure combinations of climbing/descending, banking left/right, and different headings appear across the section.

Randomly choose block figures with varying complexity. For each figure, ask for total blocks (including hidden ones). Vary height, depth, and stacking. Use isometric-style visuals via uiSpec and HTML/CSS.

selectionDetails.subtopicPool: basic_aerodynamics, aircraft_controls_and_axes, aircraft_components_and_systems, helicopter_basics, basic_navigation_concepts, flight_instruments_concepts, flight_operations_and_procedures
selectionDetails.rule: Draw roughly equal numbers of items from each AI subtopic. Use clear, non-classified, high-level aviation knowledge suitable for public test prep.

navigationFlow.sectionTransition: After finishing each section (time expires or user submits all answers), show a 'Section Complete' summary screen with score for that section (where applicable) and a 'Continue' button. Once user confirms, load the next section in the order above with its own timer.
navigationFlow.examCompletion: At the end of Aviation Information, show a full test summary page with per-section accuracy, timing, and composite score breakdown.

compositeScoring.notes: This app uses percentage-correct by section to approximate composites; it does NOT replicate the Air Force’s proprietary scaled-score formulas. For training purposes, composite scores are computed as the average percent-correct of their contributing subtests.

Verbal.calculationRule: Average percent correct across the three subtests.

Quantitative.calculationRule: Average percent correct across AR and MK.

AcademicAptitude.calculationRule: Average percent correct across the four subtests.

Pilot.calculationRule: Average percent correct across the four subtests.

CSO.calculationRule: Average percent correct across the six subtests.

ABM.calculationRule: Average percent correct across the six subtests.

copilotImplementationNotes.difficultyBinding: When user chooses Beginner/Advanced/Expert Full Exam, bind the difficulty field for every section’s question selection to that difficulty.
copilotImplementationNotes.randomization: Every exam run must re-sample questions. No question id may appear more than once within a single full exam instance.
copilotImplementationNotes.timers: Each section uses a dedicated countdown timer based on timeLimitSeconds. Once timer hits zero, section auto-submits unanswered items as blank.
copilotImplementationNotes.persistence: Store per-question references back to original JSON file & id for review mode and analytics (e.g., which subtopics user is weak on).
